final.title: The Light She Carries Across
final.logline: A large glowing orb is pressed under a dark swell while the goddess watches over it calmly, then her raised palm settles the water and a line of starlight carries the orb away across the sea.
final.hook: A big warm orb flickers in the lower foreground on black water while the goddess's third eye glows steadily above it, and a dark swell rises from the left and splashes over the orb, which dims to a trembling glow but stays visible.
final.story: This beat shows protection from sudden danger and crossing over, which fits the readings of Her name as the star that guides, the saviour, and the one who ferries across the ocean of worldly existence. The orb is a plain, open symbol of a light, a soul, a devotee, anyone in the dark, and the caption says so. The dark water stands for the ocean of existence. She is shown watching over the orb from the first frame: Her third eye already glows and Her gaze rests on the light with calm attention, so She never reads as a bystander. The danger is brief and the orb never goes fully dark. Her response is to settle the water, not to fight it. Her palm lifts and the swell draws back and flattens, which echoes the poison-sea story of soothing rather than smiting. One continuous line of starlight then fades up beneath the orb and carries it away toward the horizon. The fierce side is Her steady, unflinching gaze and Her glowing third eye. The gentle side is the settled water and the safe passage. Review notes for the human reviewer: (1) the open raised palm is an invented stylization, since the sources give scissors, skull cup, sword, blue lotus or knife in the hands, and it is used once in this clip, so please confirm or swap it; (2) the orb is an invented symbol, named in the caption; (3) the maternal reading is a devotional view and not a universal one, so the caption names both the fierce and the mother side; (4) the etymology varies by source; (5) the anchor's loose hair is left as it is.
final.loop: The last frame matches the first. After the first orb has been carried away to a distant star point, a second orb of the same size and brightness drifts into the same lower foreground spot on black water, Her hand has lowered out of frame to match the portrait, and a low dark swell begins to rise from the left again. The replay reads as one more light that needs carrying, so the guidance is continuing and not a rewind.
final.share_trigger: People send it to someone going through a frightening stretch, or to a parent or friend, to say 'you will be carried across'. The orb is a clear stand-in for a person, so the message reads without knowing the goddess. The caption gives the meaning of Her name as a fact worth saving. Viewers rewatch for the moment the swell draws back and the line of starlight fades up under the orb.
final.caption_hook: Her name means the one who ferries you across. Fierce to what threatens you, Mother to those who call. Send this to someone who needs carrying (the glowing light is a soul, a devotee, anyone in the dark).
final.audio: A low, slow drone that swells gently as the dark swell rises, with soft lapping water. A single deep conch note sounds the moment Her palm lifts, then the drone settles into a calm warm tone. One soft chime sounds as the line of starlight fades up. In the last second the drone swells again very quietly as the second orb arrives, so it leads back into the opening.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium shot, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed, black water filling the lower third of the frame, with a large bright warm orb in the lower foreground from the first frame.
shots.action: The orb flickers strongly, and a dark swell rises from the left and splashes over it, so the orb dims to a trembling glow that stays visible through the water. Her third eye glows steadily and Her calm gaze rests on the orb, so She reads as watching over the light from the first moment.
shots.purpose: The stake reads at thumbnail size: a big warm light against a dark wave, with the goddess already attentive. The orb is threatened but never fully submerged, and the splash gives visible motion in the first second.

shots.camera: Eye-level medium shot, crown centered and fully framed, with a very slow steady push-in toward Her that adds momentum while keeping the orb and the water in the lower frame.
shots.action: Her open right palm lifts slowly to chest height with the fingers relaxed and the palm facing the water, so the dark swell draws back and flattens into calm water. A single continuous line of soft starlight then fades up across the water beneath the orb, so the orb floats on a glowing path that leads away to the right.
shots.purpose: One clear cause and effect: the palm lifts, the water settles, and the path of light appears. Settling the water, not defeating it, keeps the beat reverent. The path is one glowing line, so it needs no precise timing.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium shot, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed, holding steady and matching the opening framing.
shots.action: The orb glides smoothly along the line of starlight to the right and shrinks into a small star-like point on the horizon, so the crossing reads as complete. A second orb of the same size and brightness drifts in from the left and settles in the lower foreground where the first orb began, while Her hand lowers slowly out of frame so the portrait view matches the opening, and a low dark swell begins to rise behind the new orb.
shots.purpose: The payoff is safe passage, shown as one move. The second orb and the matching framing make the last frame resemble the first, so the loop reads as guidance that continues.

concept.title: The Path Appears
concept.logline: From the very first second She raises Her open hand over the black water, and a road of starlight unspools across the sea toward the viewer.
concept.hook: At 0.0s Her open hand starts rising and a ring of ripples spreads from the shore at Her feet across the black water. By 1.5s a thin thread of starlight is already drawing itself toward the viewer.
concept.story: Her role is the one who ferries people across the ocean of worldly existence. The clip is a single act of guidance. The dark water offers no way through until She lifts Her hand, and then a road forms and is held open for the viewer to follow. She stays calm and certain, and the stillness of the sea is the proof of Her protection.
concept.loop: The path dims into faint glimmers, Her hand returns to Her side and the water settles into the calm black mirror of the opening frame. The guiding star above the crown glows as it did at the start, so the last frame leads straight back into the first lift of the hand.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to a friend who is facing something uncertain, with the message 'there is a way through, keep walking'. It also works as a gentle good-night message to someone anxious.
concept.caption_hook: When you cannot see the way across, She makes one.
concept.audio: Deep, slow low drone. Soft lapping water. A single clear bell note when the path of starlight forms, then one sustained warm female hum that fades out at the end to meet the start.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her open right hand rises slowly from Her side, and as Her palm turns toward the water a ring of soft ripples spreads outward from the shore at Her feet and a faint thread of starlight begins to glimmer on the surface.
shots.purpose: Motion begins on the first frame so the hook lands inside 1.5 seconds, and the first gesture already causes a visible effect.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her hand extends forward with the palm open over the dark water, and a narrow path of starlight spreads across the surface toward the viewer while concentric ripples widen on both sides of it. Her heavy black hair settles slowly under its own weight after the movement.
shots.purpose: This is the payoff: the road of light is the central image and the clearest promise of guidance on a phone screen.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her hand lowers slowly to Her side, and the path of starlight dims into scattered glimmers as the water flattens back into a calm black mirror. The guiding star above the crown glows a little brighter as the surface goes still.
shots.purpose: Returns to the opening composition so the clip loops cleanly, and it leaves a feeling of safe passage.

feedback: virality: Hook is a slow hand rise plus faint ripples and a 'thin thread' of starlight. Motion starts at 0.0s but it is low contrast and low stakes. On a phone, soft ripples and a thread are hard to read in 1.5s.

virality: The payoff (a glowing road) is the most common AI-devotional visual: 'goddess raises hand, light appears'. Little novelty and no tension. The water offers no problem before the path appears, so the viewer has no question to hold them.

virality: Three static, identical medium close-ups with a hand rising and lowering. The road is drawn 'toward the viewer' from a front-facing close-up, so the perspective is hard to read: how a path reads on the water from a chest-up frame is unclear.

virality: Loop is a fade-out to calm, which ends on a dim, low-energy frame. The path vanishing erases the payoff just as it lands, so people have no reason to rewatch. Resetting to the opening frame is clean but not compelling.
virality: Weak save value: nothing to retain beyond the caption line. Send-worthiness rests on the generic 'there is a way through' message, which is decent but easily met by any comfort clip.
virality: Ignores iconography beyond the open hand: no scissors, no ocean-crossing figure, no corpse or Shiva. 'Goddess stands there and gestures' is exactly the pattern to avoid.

authenticity: The concept is the generic 'goddess raises a hand and light appears' gesture, which is close to the 'standing still and raising a hand' pose the dossier warns against. The dossier asks for a beat that shows her saving or guiding. This shows guidance but not rescue, and there is no one in danger.
authenticity: It leans on the 'ferries across' etymology without saying that the dossier lists three readings of the name. Presenting one reading as the definitive meaning slightly overstates it.

authenticity: Nothing in it is specifically Tara. The ocean, the path of stars and the hand could belong to any benevolent goddess. There is no scissors, no cremation-ground or corpse iconography, and no Ugra or protective-from-sudden-danger aspect. Her wrathful, fierce side is erased, so she reads as a soft, generic guide.

authenticity: The hair is described as 'heavy black hair' settling. This reuses the anchor's loose hair, which the dossier flags as departing from the jata or Ekajata braid. The concept draws attention to the discrepancy instead of resolving it.
authenticity: Caption and share copy ('There is a way through, keep walking') is self-help framing and slightly secularises her purpose. It never mentions mercy or the devotee-child relationship.

authenticity: The audio asks for a 'warm female hum' and a bell, a neutral new-age sound palette. It has no devotional or tantric grounding, such as mantra or conch, and could read as a meditation-app aesthetic.
feasibility: Three 'shots' are written as a 3/4/3 split, but Seedance renders one continuous 10s clip. Per-shot timing is only a loose guide and will not be obeyed to the second.
feasibility: The 1.5s hook is unreliable. Ripples, a starlight thread and a hand rise all landing in the first 1.5s is a lot, and image-to-video usually eases in from the reference frame.

feasibility: A road of starlight 'unspooling toward the viewer' on a static, front-facing camera is a perspective-heavy effect. It may render as a flat glowing strip, a lit shoreline or a shimmering reflection rather than a clear path.
feasibility: Hand extending 'forward toward the viewer' with the palm open means foreshortening, which often distorts fingers and hands. The anchor has no held objects, which helps.

feasibility: Ending on a hair settle, a dimming path, a star glow and calm water in the last 3s is several simultaneous small changes. Exact loop closure to the first frame is not guaranteed, and the star glow is a subtle change that may not read.

feasibility: Cause and effect is mostly clear (hand raised, then path), which is a strength. 'Settles under its own weight' for the hair is hard to control, and the anchor has loose flowing hair that may drift unpredictably.
feasibility: The 'ring of ripples from the shore at Her feet' assumes her feet are visible, but a medium close-up with crown fully framed may crop them out, so the source of the ripples is ambiguous.

virality fix: Open on a problem, not calm: black water with no way across, with a visible, high-contrast event in the first 1s (e.g. a single star falls and strikes the water, or the hand snaps open and the path shoots outward in 0.5s).
virality fix: Make the path build in distinct, countable steps (stepping stones of light lighting up one by one toward the viewer) so the viewer anticipates the next one and stays to the end.

virality fix: Keep the road lit at the end rather than dimming, then have the last stone/star lift up into the third eye or crown star, which feeds directly into the first frame's glow. This makes a causal loop rather than a fade.
virality fix: Add a small mid-clip turn (the water bucks or darkens once, her hand holds, the path completes) to create tension and a reason to rewatch.
virality fix: Add one iconographic detail (a skull-garland or blue lotus that blooms where the first stone lands) to give novelty and a save-worthy reveal.

authenticity fix: Keep the open hand but add one signature Tara element in frame, such as the third eye glowing as the path forms, or a faint tiger-skin and skull-garland detail, so it is unmistakably her and not a generic goddess.
authenticity fix: Show a small, unnamed rescue moment, such as a single drifting light or lamp on the dark water that the path carries to safety, so the beat is a rescue and not only a gesture.
authenticity fix: Soften the etymology claim in the caption or notes ('one of her names means the one who ferries across') and avoid stating it as the sole meaning.
authenticity fix: Match the hair to the dossier (matted jata or single braid) or note the anchor deviation for human review. Do not highlight loose hair in the action text.
authenticity fix: Replace the generic hum and bell with something drawn from the tradition, such as a soft conch or a restrained mantra-like tone, and avoid chanting actual mantras casually.
feasibility fix: Write it as one continuous action: slow hand rise, then water shimmer, then a glowing path on the water. Drop the per-second timestamps and the 1.5s hook claim.
feasibility fix: Cut the ripples at Her feet. Keep one effect: a single luminous path of light on the water receding away from the camera, with gentle ripples.
feasibility fix: Keep the palm raised and slightly forward rather than reaching at the lens, or have the hand sweep sideways across the water to avoid foreshortening.
feasibility fix: Drop the star-glow and hair-settle beats. Let the end be a simple fade of the path and a lowered hand, and accept an approximate loop.
feasibility fix: Check that the framing actually shows the water and shore in the reference portrait. If it does not, use a wider framing.

concept.title: The Sea Goes Still
concept.logline: Dark currents gather in the water behind Her, and one open palm calms them until the sea becomes a mirror of stars.
concept.hook: At 0.0s dark currents begin to turn slowly in the water behind Her while Her hand rises. By 1.5s the nearest swell visibly slows as Her palm opens toward it.
concept.story: This draws on the story of the poisoned ocean, in which She is the one who calms what is overwhelming and rescues the one who is suffering. The unrest is the viewer's own trouble. Her open hand does not fight the water. It settles it, and the stars return only once the water is still.
concept.loop: The mirror-calm sea at the end matches the calm black ocean of the opening frame. The last quiet ripple lifts from the shore at Her feet, which is how the clip begins, so the unrest gathering again at the start feels like the next wave of the same cycle.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to someone who is overwhelmed, burned out or grieving, as a quiet 'breathe, this will settle'. It is also easy to save as a calming clip for a bad night.
concept.caption_hook: Some storms only need to be met with a steady hand.
concept.audio: Low rumbling swell that softens into silence as the water calms. Gentle water lapping. A soft rising choir pad with one sustained held note at the end.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Dark currents turn slowly in the black water behind Her and small swells lap at the shore, while Her open hand rises gently and the nearest swell slows as Her palm turns toward it.
shots.purpose: Shows visible, specific motion in the first frame and sets up the problem the viewer will want to see solved.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her palm opens fully over the water, and the dark currents unwind and flatten into a smooth mirror in which the cold distant stars appear one by one. Her hair settles slowly under its own weight as the motion ends.
shots.purpose: The payoff: calm spreading across the water and stars arriving give a satisfying release that holds viewers to the end.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her hand lowers to Her side, and the guiding star above the crown is reflected as a single steady gleam in the still water while one last soft ripple drifts out from the shore.
shots.purpose: Returns to the opening composition for a seamless loop, with a final quiet moment of rest.

feedback: virality: Strongest story: unrest to calm is a clear problem-and-resolution arc, tied to the poison/ocean myth, and gives the viewer an open question ('will it settle?') that holds to the end.

virality: Hook is still gentle: 'dark currents turning slowly' and a swell that 'slows'. Slow turning water is hard to read in 1.5s on a phone and may look like a static scene. Needs a more violent, high-contrast start for the calm to feel earned.

virality: Same static front-facing close-up for all 10s with the hand rising and lowering; gesture-driven. The payoff (water flattening and stars appearing one by one) is pretty but predictable, and the 'stars appear in the mirror' is a stock image.

virality: Loop logic is muddled: the clip opens on turbulent currents but the ending is a calm mirror, and the caption of loop says the opening is 'calm black ocean'. Opening and closing frames do not actually match, so the seam would be visible. The 'unrest gathering again' is claimed but not shown.
virality: Shot 3 is only 2s of resting with a single ripple: a low-energy ending that risks swipe-away right before the loop.
virality: Audio relies on a rumble that fades to silence, so the loop point has a dead audio gap unless it is designed to restart with the rumble.

authenticity: The poison-story link is the right source, but the concept does not flag that this legend is devotional-tradition material, not in the main Puranic accounts, and that the dossier notes variants (Durga or Parvati, or Tara taking the poison herself). The text says 'the story of the poisoned ocean' as if canonical. Add a hedge in notes or caption.

authenticity: The 'unrest is the viewer's own trouble' reading is a modern psychological gloss. It is mostly harmless, but it moves away from the actual myth, in which she rescues Shiva, and the concept never mentions that.

authenticity: Her calming of the sea is her gesture alone. The story's emotional core is the nurturing mother, and the open palm does not carry it. A devotee might find a stern, aloof posture less true than the maternal protectiveness at the center of the Tarapith and Bamakhepa tradition.
authenticity: Her hair settles 'under its own weight', which still emphasises the loose-hair anchor deviation.

authenticity: 'Cold distant stars' and the mirror-of-stars ending are pretty but aesthetic. Nothing marks it as Tara and not any sea goddess. The caption ('Some storms only need to be met with a steady hand') is generic and drops the saviour/mother meaning.
authenticity: The choir pad is Western-sacred and mixes in a church-style sound, a small tradition-mixing risk.

feasibility: 'Dark currents turning slowly' behind Her and 'the nearest swell slows as the palm turns toward it' ask the model to show a physical process of water slowing down, with a cause that is only implied by a gesture. Video models tend to render water as constantly moving and may not show a legible calming.
feasibility: Stars appearing 'one by one' in the reflection is a sequential, many-element effect. It will likely pop in all at once or flicker.

feasibility: The 'swell slows' beat and the 'currents unwind and flatten' beat are subtle and hard to prompt. The result may look like generic water with a raised hand and no visible link between them.

feasibility: The 4/4/2 shot split is not honoured by a single 10s generation. The last 2s carries three micro-events: the hand lowering, a star reflection and one last ripple. That is too much for 2s.

feasibility: The loop depends on the water starting turbulent and ending calm. That conflicts with the claimed seamless loop, because the first frame has unrest and the last is mirror-calm. The 'next wave of the same cycle' argument is a stretch.
feasibility: Water behind Her means a background change with Her in the foreground, so reference-image consistency (the background of the portrait) is at risk.
virality fix: Make the first second violent and legible: black water heaving with dark tendrils or smoke-like poison streaks lunging at the frame, so the contrast with the calm is dramatic.

virality fix: Make the calming physical and traceable: her palm moves along the water and a visible line of stillness follows it, with the dark streaks draining away or sinking out of frame, so the viewer watches the problem get solved in real time.

virality fix: Fix the loop: end with the final dark streak or one new swell stirring at the far edge as the stars appear, so the last frame matches the unrest of the first. Or open on the calm mirror and let the first frame disturb it.
virality fix: Trim the resting shot and spend those seconds on the stars appearing with a clear beat sync (one chime per star) for rhythm and rewatch value.
virality fix: Optionally let the third eye flash at the moment the water stops, a single hard visual punctuation that makes the payoff screenshot-worthy.
authenticity fix: Add a note that the poison rescue is a devotional tradition with variants, and keep it implicit (a calmed sea) without naming Shiva or the goddess's identity as settled fact.
authenticity fix: Rework the caption to carry her maternal protection, for example 'She stills what burns,' or 'The Mother who calms the burning,' in place of the generic 'steady hand' line.
authenticity fix: Add a soft, caring quality to the gesture (a slow, gentle palm, a calm expression) so it reads as maternal compassion and not command.
authenticity fix: Replace the choir pad with a drone, a low tanpura-like tone or a gentle conch.
authenticity fix: Resolve the hair issue (jata or braid) or flag it for human review.

feasibility fix: Simplify to two states: choppy dark water at the start, then smooth water with a soft star-shimmer at the end. Do not specify stars arriving individually, just 'stars become visible in the water'.
feasibility fix: Make the calming cause visible: the palm sweeps slowly and horizontally, and the ripples visibly flatten outward from her hand.
feasibility fix: Drop the final ripple and star-gleam beats. End on the still water and a lowered hand.
feasibility fix: Accept that this will not loop seamlessly, or open on a mildly agitated surface and end on calm, with a crossfade planned in the edit rather than in the generation.

concept.title: Your Turn to Cross
concept.logline: The camera glides back along the road of starlight she opens, so the viewer feels they are standing at the start of the crossing, then returns to Her face.
concept.hook: At 0.0s a soft glow gathers at Her third eye and starlight spreads in a line across the water at Her feet. By 1.5s the camera has begun a slow glide backward along that line.
concept.story: Her name is read as star, saviour and the one who ferries across. Here the camera is the traveller. She opens the path with a gesture, and the camera is carried out over the water along it, so the viewer feels guided. The return to Her face at the end says She is still watching over the crossing.
concept.loop: At the end the camera glides gently forward to the original portrait framing, Her hand returns to Her side and the path folds back into the single guiding star above Her crown. That is the same face, framing and stillness as the first frame, ready for the glow at Her third eye to begin again.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to someone starting something new, such as a move, a job or a recovery, with the message 'you are not crossing alone'. It also suits anyone who likes a 'POV, you are being guided' feeling.
concept.caption_hook: POV: you are being carried across.
concept.audio: Soft wind-like air pad with distant water. A slow rising string tone as the camera glides back, a single bell when the path appears, and a warm low hum as the camera glides forward to Her face.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: A soft blue-white glow gathers at the vertical third eye, and a thin line of starlight spreads across the wet sand and dark water at Her feet. Her open hand begins to rise, causing ripples to widen from that line.
shots.purpose: Starts motion in the first frame and plants the path as the central image before the camera moves.

shots.camera: Slow, smooth glide backward at eye level, keeping the crown centered and fully framed, widening the view without any tilt.
shots.action: Her hand extends over the water and the path of starlight stretches far toward the horizon, with concentric ripples spreading on both sides. The camera drifts back along the path, so the distance of the crossing becomes visible while Her hair settles slowly.
shots.purpose: A gentle pull-back changes the scale and gives the viewer a sense of travelling, which helps retention and novelty over a static portrait.

shots.camera: Slow, smooth glide forward at eye level, returning to the original face-and-upper-body framing with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: The camera glides forward to Her face as Her hand lowers to Her side, and the path of starlight folds back toward the single guiding star above Her crown, leaving the water calm and dark.
shots.purpose: Brings the clip back to the opening portrait for a clean loop and ends on Her steady gaze.

feedback: virality: Camera move is the only real novelty across the three concepts, but it is under-specified and risky: a glide back 'along the path' while keeping the crown centered and framed means the goddess shrinks or the background just rescales, with no clear parallax. In AI video this often renders as a zoom or a warping figure.

virality: Hook is a soft glow at the third eye and a thin line of starlight on wet sand; shot 1 is described as a static camera, so the claim that the camera begins gliding by 1.5s contradicts the shot list. The first 1.5s is a faint glow, not strong motion.
virality: Retention is weaker than the pitch: the pull-back reveals a long path, but nothing happens at the end of that path (no destination, no reveal), so the payoff is just 'more road'.

virality: The loop requires the camera to glide forward to an identical framing; any drift in face, hair or framing will show a seam. The camera ends on a calm, dark frame like A, so it carries the same low-energy ending.

virality: Concept is the weakest on clarity for a single 10s clip: static, glide back, glide forward is a lot of mechanics for 10s and the 'POV carried across' idea is not delivered since the viewer sees her from the front throughout rather than from the traveller's view.
virality: Shares A's generic goddess-raises-hand-and-light-appears core.

authenticity: The camera spec is internally inconsistent. Shot 1 is 'static', the loop section says the camera 'glides gently forward to the original portrait framing', and shot 2 pulls back 'with the crown centered and fully framed'. Pulling back while the crown stays fully framed and the face stays readable is physically contradictory, and the dossier's note about a 'locked anchor' makes the changing frame risky. This is a production and consistency flaw as well.

authenticity: The POV conceit ('you are being carried across') puts the viewer into the role of the one being ferried, which is close to the devotional meaning. However, 'carried' and the camera as traveller turns a sacred figure's act of grace into a ride, which edges toward a gimmick and the 'POV' meme format. A devotee may find the 'POV' framing trivialising.

authenticity: The share trigger ('you are not crossing alone' for a move or a job) is secular motivational use. It is acceptable, but it does not touch her actual domains: sudden danger, suffering, knowledge.
authenticity: It leans on the three-way etymology ('star, saviour and the one who ferries') and states all three as her name's meaning without noting that sources differ.
authenticity: Like A, it has no distinctive Tara iconography beyond the third eye and star. The wrathful, tantric character is absent entirely.
authenticity: 'Wet sand and dark water at Her feet' is vague. The cremation-ground and corpse imagery is rightly skipped as sensitive, but nothing replaces it that says 'Tara'.
authenticity: The audio set (wind pad, strings, bell, hum) is generic cinematic music with no cultural grounding.

feasibility: Calls for a camera glide backward, then a glide forward back to the original framing, within a single 10s clip. A reversal of camera motion mid-clip is unreliable in image-to-video and often yields a drift rather than a return.

feasibility: The pull-back must reveal new scene content (a horizon, a long path, a wider shore) that does not exist in the reference portrait. The model has to invent the whole environment while keeping Her face and crown consistent.

feasibility: Camera moving while the crown stays 'centered and fully framed', combined with 'widening the view without any tilt', is contradictory. Widening reduces Her size in frame, so crown-centred framing and a wide reveal conflict.
feasibility: Shot 1 is labelled 'static' while the hook claims a camera glide begins by 1.5s. The brief contradicts itself.
feasibility: The returning glide must land on the exact original framing for the loop. Image-to-video will not reliably match the first frame at the end.
feasibility: Too many simultaneous elements in shot 2: hand extension, a path stretching to the horizon, concentric ripples on both sides, camera movement and hair settling.

feasibility: The third-eye glow and the 'path folds back toward the guiding star above Her crown' are abstract transformations with no physical logic. The star-above-crown is not established as part of the anchor either.
feasibility: The 'POV, you are being carried across' premise implies the viewer moves, but the camera moves away from Her, which reads as retreating rather than being carried.
virality fix: Fix the shot-1 camera note so it matches the claim: start the pull-back at 0.0s, with no static opening.

virality fix: Commit to a real POV: start tight on her face and pull back fast along the path so the viewer is moving across the water, with her shrinking to a star on the horizon in a single continuous move. Then cut or whip back to the face for the loop.
virality fix: Put a payoff at the end of the path: the far horizon reveals something specific (a lit shore, a lotus, a doorway of stars) so the pull-back answers 'where does it lead?'.

virality fix: Keep the face locked and the move simple (one dolly, no second glide) to avoid warping and to cut mechanics; use the freed time for a stronger first second, such as a hard blue flash from the third eye as the line of light shoots out.
virality fix: Make the loop a match-cut: the final forward glide lands on the exact opening glow, with the audio hum resolving into the opening bell.

authenticity fix: Make the camera spec consistent: either a true locked portrait with the path unfolding in the water, or a defined pull-back that explicitly allows the crown to leave the frame, and state that the face and iconography remain legible.
authenticity fix: Drop the 'POV' caption and replace it with a reverent line such as 'She carries across what you cannot cross alone,' or one that names her as the one who ferries across.
authenticity fix: Soften the etymology in notes and caption ('among her names: star, saviour, the one who ferries across').

concept.title: The Little Light Carried Across
concept.logline: A small light is dragged across black water by dark currents, and Tara's open hand lights stepping stones one by one until the light is carried safely over.
concept.hook: A bright star drops from the night sky and strikes the black water beside Her, throwing a high-contrast ring of light across the surface. The ring shows a tiny light being dragged away by dark currents, and Her third eye brightens as Her hand starts to rise.

The water bucks and darkens once, Her hand holds steady, and the stones keep lighting. A blue lotus blooms where the first stone lands. The glow of the stones softly reveals Her tiger-skin wrap and skull garland, so she reads as Tara and not a generic goddess. She is shown as a mother who will not let Her child go under. concept.loop: The road of stones stays lit at the end. The rescued light rises from the last stone into Her third eye, which holds the soft glow seen in the first frame. concept.title: She Stills What Burns
concept.logline: Black poison-streaked water surges toward the viewer, and Her slow, gentle palm sweeps across it, leaving a trail of still water and rising stars.
concept.hook: The first frame is the calm black water behind Her. By 0.5s dark smoke-like streaks burst up from it and heave the surface into sharp, choppy waves that lunge toward the viewer, while Her open hand begins to rise. By 1.5s the waves are visibly violent against Her calm, soft-eyed face.
concept.story: The ocean-poison legend is devotional tradition. It is not in the main Puranic accounts, and its versions differ: in some She takes the poison herself, and in some another goddess does. The clip keeps it implicit and names no one: a sea of poison rages, and the Mother calms it. In that tradition She is the protective mother who ferries others across danger. Her palm moves slowly and gently, with a caring face, so it reads as compassion and not command. The viewer watches the problem get solved in real time: a line of stillness follows her hand, the dark streaks sink, and only then do the stars show in the water. Hair note for human review: the anchor has loose hair, while tradition shows matted hair or a single braid. The clip keeps Her hair hanging quietly and does not draw attention to it.
concept.loop: The clip opens on the calm black water of the anchor frame and ends on that same calm black water, with a faint star shimmer. The surge erupts in the first half-second of every replay, so the end flows into the start as the next storm of the same cycle. A short crossfade in the edit can smooth the seam if the final water level differs slightly from the opening frame.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to someone who is overwhelmed, burned out or grieving, as a quiet 'breathe, it will settle'. The violent start and the clear, satisfying calming make it a clip to rewatch and save for a bad night.
concept.caption_hook: The Mother who calms what burns.
concept.audio: Opens at once on a low rumbling swell with a deep pulse as the streaks surge, so the loop restarts on sound. As the palm sweeps, the rumble thins and a low, sustained string drone rises underneath. Soft bell-like chimes sound as the stars become visible, followed by one soft, low conch note that carries into the next replay's rumble.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed. The water sits behind Her at the same horizon and framing as the reference portrait.
shots.action: From the calm black water, dark smoke-like streaks burst upward and heave the surface into sharp, choppy waves that lunge toward the frame, while Her face stays calm and soft-eyed and Her open hand rises slowly to chest height with the palm facing the water, which makes the nearest streaks bend away from it.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.

shots.purpose: The calming is physical and traceable: the viewer sees the cause (her palm) and the effect (a line of stillness) in real time. The third-eye glow is the single punctuation that makes the payoff screenshot-worthy.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her hand lowers gently to Her side with a warm, maternal expression, and the now-still black water takes on a soft shimmer as stars become visible in it, ending on calm water that matches the opening frame.
shots.purpose: A short, satisfying release with one clear beat on the chimes. It ends on the same calm water the clip began with, so the replay jumps straight into the next surge.

virality: The payoff is clean and traceable: palm sweeps, a band of stillness follows, streaks sink. This is a satisfying cause-and-effect and gives a strong hold, since people stay to see the whole surface calm.

concept.title: She Calms the Poisoned Sea
concept.logline: Dark poison currents churn the water behind Her, flashes of cold light reveal Her skull garland, tiger-skin wrap and serpent ornaments, and Her open palm settles the sea and draws a path of starlight toward the viewer.
concept.hook: The first frame is the reference portrait, with calm black water behind Her. From the first instant, dark currents rise in the water behind and below Her, and the surface roils into choppy waves. Pale blue-white flashes inside the currents light up Her skull garland, tiger-skin wrap and the serpent coiled at Her neck, and the serpent's jewelled eyes glint. Her three eyes stay steady and stern, and by 1s Her open palm lifts to chest height.
concept.story: Tara is the star that guides and the saviour who ferries across the ocean of existence. This clip shows that meaning as one clear sequence: a sea of poison churns, Her steady gaze and open palm settle it, and a path of starlight forms across the calm water toward the viewer. The poison story belongs to one devotional tradition and is not in the main Puranic accounts. Versions differ on which goddess acts, so nothing in the visuals names anyone and the caption carries a hedge. Her protective, wrathful side stays visible through a stern, unflinching expression and the lit skull garland, tiger-skin wrap and serpent ornaments, so She reads as Tara and not a generic gentle mother. Her palm does not command the sea alone. The water settles under Her gaze as the hand opens, then the path appears and stays. Hair note for human review: the anchor has loose hair, while tradition shows matted hair or a single braid. The clip lets Her hair hang and settle gradually under gravity and does not draw attention to it. Held objects (scissors, skull cup, sword, blue lotus) are omitted so the hands stay simple. Human review should confirm that is acceptable.
concept.loop: The clip ends on calm dark water with the starlight path still glowing and a faint, steady glow from Her third eye. In the last half-second the stars soften into the dark surface and one faint current stirs, which matches the opening frame of calm black water with currents gathering. The replay picks up the same quiet stirring, so the end flows into the start as a tide that returns and not as a reset that undoes the rescue. The starlight path is the last strong image the viewer holds.
concept.share_trigger: Devotees and people who love Tara send it as a picture of her as guide and saviour: the one who calms the dark water and lights a way across. People going through a hard stretch send it to a friend as 'there is a way across'. The caption's one line of legend, labelled as one tradition, gives viewers a reason to save it and look up the story.
concept.caption_hook: In one devotional tradition, the Mother calms the poisoned sea and lights the way across.
concept.audio: Opens straight into a low, soft rumble with a slow deep pulse as the currents rise. A low string drone grows under it as Her palm moves. When the water settles, the rumble thins to silence and soft bell-like chimes sound one by one as the stars form the path. One low, soft conch note ends the clip and carries gently into the restart.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed. The water sits behind Her at the same horizon and framing as the reference portrait.

Her third eye gives one soft glow that lights the flattening water.

shots.camera: Eye-level medium close-up that eases slowly and smoothly back to a slightly wider framing, crown centered and fully framed, to show more of the still water in front of Her.

concept.title: The Light She Carries Across
concept.logline: A large, glowing orb is swallowed by a black wave, and the goddess's open hand lights a line of star-lights across the water until the orb is set down safely on the far bank.
concept.hook: A lantern-sized orb of warm light flickers in the lower foreground on black water, and a dark wave rolls in from the left and closes over it, shrinking it to a thin point of light while Her stern gaze drops to the water.
concept.story: This beat shows rescue and crossing over, which fits the readings of Her name as the one who ferries across the ocean of worldly existence, as the star that guides, and as the saviour. The sources vary on the etymology, so the orb is a plain, open symbol of a being in danger and the dark water stands for the ocean of existence. The fierce, protective side is shown directly. Her third eye brightens, a dark wave lashes up toward Her and recoils from Her gaze, and the water flattens. Her open hand then glides across the water and a path of starlight ignites in order beneath it, as in the recommended beat of the research notes. The star-lights throw a thin pale rim of light along the tiger-skin wrap and the skull garland, so Her fierce identity is clear. The crossing ends with the orb set down on the far bank and Her hand lowering, with no absorption into Her body. Review notes for the human reviewer: (1) the open-palm gesture is an invented stylization, since the sources give scissors, skull cup, sword, blue lotus or knife; (2) the reference portrait has loose hair, while the tradition shows a matted crown of hair or a single braid, so the action text leaves the hair alone except for it settling under gravity; (3) the lotus and stepping stones from the earlier draft are dropped as inventions; (4) the maternal reading is a devotional view and not a universal one.
concept.loop: The clip ends on the orb resting steady and bright on the far bank, the water calm, and Her third eye holding a soft glow that dims toward a single star-like point. The opening shows a bright orb on dark water, so the replay reads as another light that needs carrying across. The match is approximate. There is no object entering Her face, so the loop does not imply absorption.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to someone going through a frightening stretch, or to a parent, to say 'you will be carried across'. Many devotees call Her Mother and see Her as the one who ferries them over, so the clip suits that message. Viewers rewatch for the moment the dark wave recoils from Her gaze and the star-lights ignite one after another.
concept.caption_hook: Devotees call Her Mother, the one who carries you across the dark water.
concept.audio: A low, slow drone with soft lapping water. A deep rumble swells as the dark wave closes over the orb, and a deep conch note sounds as Her third eye brightens. Soft chime-like hits mark each star-light as it ignites. The conch decays into the drone in the last two seconds so it leads back into the opening swell.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed, with black water filling the lower frame from the first moment and a large glowing orb in the lower foreground.
shots.action: A dark wave rolls in from the left and closes over the flickering orb, so the orb shrinks to a thin point of light under the surface, while Her stern gaze lowers to the water and Her third eye begins to brighten, lighting the dark ripples around it.
shots.purpose: The danger reads in one glance: a big, bright light is swallowed by a wave. Motion starts on the first frame with a single event and no crowding.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed, with only a very slow, slight push-in.
shots.action: Her open right hand rises slowly into the frame with the palm facing the water, so a dark wave that lashes up toward Her recoils from Her gaze and flattens to calm water. A first star-light ignites beneath the sunken point of light and lifts the orb back to the surface, bright again. Her hand then glides slowly to the right, and one star-light after another ignites in order beneath Her passing fingertips, so a path of four star-lights carries the orb across the water toward a low pale bank at the right edge. The star-lights throw a thin rim of light along Her tiger-skin wrap and skull garland.
shots.purpose: One clear causal chain: the hand rises and the wave recoils, then the hand glides and the star-lights ignite in order. The recoiling wave shows the fierce protective side, and the rim-lit wrap and garland mark Her identity.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed, holding steady.
shots.action: The orb settles onto the last star-light at the bank and glows steadily, so the safe landing is clear. Her hand lowers slowly to Her side, so the water goes still and shows a calm path of star-lights, while Her third eye holds a soft glow that dims toward a single star-like point and Her hair settles gradually under gravity.
shots.purpose: The payoff stays visible and complete: the light is set down safely and the crossing is finished. The calm end leads back into the opening, where a new light drifts on dark water.

concept.title: The Light She Carries Across
concept.logline: A large glowing orb is pressed under a dark swell while the goddess watches over it calmly, then her raised palm settles the water and a line of starlight carries the orb away across the sea.
concept.hook: A big warm orb flickers in the lower foreground on black water while the goddess's third eye glows steadily above it, and a dark swell rises from the left and splashes over the orb, which dims to a trembling glow but stays visible.
concept.story: This beat shows protection from sudden danger and crossing over, which fits the readings of Her name as the star that guides, the saviour, and the one who ferries across the ocean of worldly existence. The orb is a plain, open symbol of a light, a soul, a devotee, anyone in the dark, and the caption says so. The dark water stands for the ocean of existence. She is shown watching over the orb from the first frame: Her third eye already glows and Her gaze rests on the light with calm attention, so She never reads as a bystander. The danger is brief and the orb never goes fully dark. Her response is to settle the water, not to fight it. Her palm lifts and the swell draws back and flattens, which echoes the poison-sea story of soothing rather than smiting. One continuous line of starlight then fades up beneath the orb and carries it away toward the horizon. The fierce side is Her steady, unflinching gaze and Her glowing third eye. The gentle side is the settled water and the safe passage. Review notes for the human reviewer: (1) the open raised palm is an invented stylization, since the sources give scissors, skull cup, sword, blue lotus or knife in the hands, and it is used once in this clip, so please confirm or swap it; (2) the orb is an invented symbol, named in the caption; (3) the maternal reading is a devotional view and not a universal one, so the caption names both the fierce and the mother side; (4) the etymology varies by source; (5) the anchor's loose hair is left as it is.
concept.loop: The last frame matches the first. After the first orb has been carried away to a distant star point, a second orb of the same size and brightness drifts into the same lower foreground spot on black water, Her hand has lowered out of frame to match the portrait, and a low dark swell begins to rise from the left again. The replay reads as one more light that needs carrying, so the guidance is continuing and not a rewind.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to someone going through a frightening stretch, or to a parent or friend, to say 'you will be carried across'. The orb is a clear stand-in for a person, so the message reads without knowing the goddess. The caption gives the meaning of Her name as a fact worth saving. Viewers rewatch for the moment the swell draws back and the line of starlight fades up under the orb.
concept.caption_hook: Her name means the one who ferries you across. Fierce to what threatens you, Mother to those who call. Send this to someone who needs carrying (the glowing light is a soul, a devotee, anyone in the dark).
concept.audio: A low, slow drone that swells gently as the dark swell rises, with soft lapping water. A single deep conch note sounds the moment Her palm lifts, then the drone settles into a calm warm tone. One soft chime sounds as the line of starlight fades up. In the last second the drone swells again very quietly as the second orb arrives, so it leads back into the opening.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium shot, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed, black water filling the lower third of the frame, with a large bright warm orb in the lower foreground from the first frame.
shots.action: The orb flickers strongly, and a dark swell rises from the left and splashes over it, so the orb dims to a trembling glow that stays visible through the water. Her third eye glows steadily and Her calm gaze rests on the orb, so She reads as watching over the light from the first moment.
shots.purpose: The stake reads at thumbnail size: a big warm light against a dark wave, with the goddess already attentive. The orb is threatened but never fully submerged, and the splash gives visible motion in the first second.

shots.camera: Eye-level medium shot, crown centered and fully framed, with a very slow steady push-in toward Her that adds momentum while keeping the orb and the water in the lower frame.
shots.action: Her open right palm lifts slowly to chest height with the fingers relaxed and the palm facing the water, so the dark swell draws back and flattens into calm water. A single continuous line of soft starlight then fades up across the water beneath the orb, so the orb floats on a glowing path that leads away to the right.
shots.purpose: One clear cause and effect: the palm lifts, the water settles, and the path of light appears. Settling the water, not defeating it, keeps the beat reverent. The path is one glowing line, so it needs no precise timing.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium shot, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed, holding steady and matching the opening framing.
shots.action: The orb glides smoothly along the line of starlight to the right and shrinks into a small star-like point on the horizon, so the crossing reads as complete. A second orb of the same size and brightness drifts in from the left and settles in the lower foreground where the first orb began, while Her hand lowers slowly out of frame so the portrait view matches the opening, and a low dark swell begins to rise behind the new orb.
shots.purpose: The payoff is safe passage, shown as one move. The second orb and the matching framing make the last frame resemble the first, so the loop reads as guidance that continues.

feedback: virality: Hook has visible motion from frame 1 (flickering orb, swell splashing over it), and the large foreground orb will read well on a phone. But it is a generic glowing orb being hit by a wave. There is no Tara-specific image in the opening beat, and she is only 'watching', which is the passive 'goddess stands there' look the rubric penalises.

virality: The orb is a vaguer symbol than a small light being tossed on the sea. 'A glowing orb' is the most common AI-devotional-clip prop. The caption has to explain it ('the glowing light is a soul'), which signals that the visual does not carry the meaning by itself.

virality: The danger is mild by design: the orb is never fully submerged and the splash is brief. Stakes are low, so the payoff when the water settles is weak. The orb 'dims to a trembling glow but stays visible' removes the feeling that anything could be lost.

virality: Shot 2 is the whole clip's core, and it is the same palm-lift gesture over a swell. The swell 'draws back and flattens' is a slow, soft event with no impact, and a slow push-in does not fix that. 4 seconds on a slow palm-lift is a slow-middle risk.
virality: Poison story is not legible at all: no colour change, no cue. This reads as generic 'goddess calms storm' with no Tara-specific cue beyond the portrait.

virality: Loop is the best part: a second orb arriving and a new swell rising is a clever, continuous loop that implies more people to carry and makes rewatching feel purposeful. But it is a lot to land in the last 3s while the first orb is also shrinking to a horizon point and the hand is lowering, and the new swell starting 'behind the new orb' is easy to miss.

virality: Send-worthiness is decent ('you will be carried across', orb as a person stand-in), and the orb needs no myth knowledge. Save value is lower than a concept with a clear fact or reveal: the name-meaning caption is the only keepsake.
virality: Caption hook is long and tries to cover fierce, mother, send and explain the orb at once, which weakens each part.
authenticity: The open raised palm is an invented gesture in place of the dossier's held objects. The concept flags it and uses it once, but it still carries the key beat.

authenticity: The loose hair is left as is, and the concept notes it, but no commitment is made to fix the anchor before final. Devotees familiar with Tara's matted jata or Ekajata braid will see the departure.

authenticity: The orb is a symbol outside the tradition, but it is plainly named in the caption as a soul, a devotee or anyone in the dark. That is honest and works. The risk is only the 'soul' reading drifting toward a generic spirit-guide trope.

authenticity: The poison story is hinted at ('echoes the poison-sea story') but the caption never mentions it, so the ocean-of-existence reading dominates. authenticity: The caption 'Mother to those who call' is a devotional view and is not hedged in the caption itself, though the review note says the caption names both sides. authenticity: Looping to a second orb with a new swell implies endless danger, which fits ferrying across but is a slightly bleak note. It reads as guidance continuing, which is acceptable.
authenticity: The 'splash over the orb' is a peril moment, but non-graphic and the orb is never extinguished, which is respectful.

The final shot packs in the orb departing, the second orb arriving, the hand exiting, and a new swell, which is too much for 3 seconds.

feasibility: The slow push-in in shot 2 contradicts the static framing of shots 1 and 3, so the final frame will not match the opening framing. Camera moves also risk drifting her crown out of frame.

feasibility: A second orb that is identical in size and brightness and lands in the same spot is a continuity demand that models do not reliably meet, though if it fails the clip still reads acceptably.
feasibility: The orb shrinking into a star point on the horizon needs perspective depth that a front-facing medium shot with the water in the lower third does not clearly provide.

concept.title: The Light Across the Dark Water
concept.logline: A huge violet-black surge rears up behind Her over a single small light on the water, Her steady gaze and third eye stop it mid-rise, Her open palm settles the whole sea, and a line of stars carries the small light to a far shore.
concept.hook: The first frame is the reference portrait. From the first instant a towering violet-black surge rears up on both sides of Her head with a sickly violet glow along its edge, and its crest leans forward over one small warm light tossing on the dark water at the bottom of the frame. Her three eyes stay steady, and a soft bell chime sounds under the rumble. The viewer immediately asks whether the small light will be swallowed.
concept.story: Tara is the star that guides, the saviour, and the one who ferries across the ocean of existence. In one devotional tradition She also calms the poison that rose from the churning of the ocean. Versions differ on which goddess acts, so nothing in the visuals names anyone, and the caption carries the hedge because the clip has no on-screen text. The poison is made legible by a sickly violet glow in the surge that turns to clean silver-blue when the water calms. The small drifting light gives the viewer someone to worry about. The order puts the agency in Her presence: Her gaze and third eye stop the surge first, and the open palm follows as a protective gesture. Her stern unflinching face keeps Her wrathful, protective side visible, so She reads as Tara and not a generic gentle mother. The far shore light makes the path read as a crossing. Reviewer notes: (1) The raised palm is a stylised stand-in for Her held objects (scissors, skull cup, sword, blue lotus), which are omitted because held objects are hard to render. Please confirm this is acceptable. (2) The anchor has loose hair, while tradition shows matted hair or a single braid (Ekajata). Please confirm whether the anchor will be replaced before final production. In this clip Her hair hangs and settles gradually under gravity.
concept.loop: In the last second the stars dim to a few points, the small light reaches the far shore, and the water behind Her returns to the calm black of the reference portrait, with the third-eye glow steady. The replay opens on that same calm frame, and the surge rising again reads as a new storm and a new crossing. The end matches the first frame, so the seam is hidden.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to a friend going through a dark stretch such as a night shift, a long illness, grief or a hard move, with the message 'you are the small light, and there is a way across'. Devotees send it as a picture of Tara as guide and saviour. The caption's one-line meaning of Her name gives viewers a fact to save.
concept.caption_hook: Her name means star, saviour and the one who ferries you across. Send this to someone crossing a dark stretch. (In one devotional tradition, She calms the poisoned sea.)
concept.audio: Opens straight into a low, soft rumble with a slow deep pulse, and a single soft bell chime in the first second hints at the guiding star. The rumble swells as the surge rears, then drops away at the palm beat. A hush follows, then soft bell-like chimes sound one by one as the stars form the path. One low, soft conch note ends the clip and carries into the restart.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, front-facing, crown centered and fully framed. The framing is wide enough to show the water below Her shoulders and the full height of the surge on both sides of Her head.
shots.action: A huge violet-black surge rears up on both sides of Her head, and its glowing violet edge lights the water and Her blue skin. The surge leans forward over a small warm light tossing at the bottom of the frame. Her third eye glows brighter, which stops the surge mid-rise so it hangs trembling above Her shoulders. Her three eyes stay steady and stern, and Her hair hangs and settles gradually under gravity.
shots.purpose: A large, high-contrast event in frame 1 with a clear stake: the small light is about to be swallowed. One effect, a rearing surge, reads instantly on a phone. The third-eye glow stopping it shows that Her gaze acts first.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her open right palm lifts steadily to chest height and stops, facing the viewer, which makes the hanging surge sink flat across the whole sea in one beat. The violet glow in the water turns to clean silver-blue, and the small light stops tossing and steadies on the calm surface.
shots.purpose: A sharp cause-and-effect beat with a forward-facing palm that does not cross the torso or ornaments. The sea going flat is the payoff of the stakes, the poison turning silver makes the rescue legible, and the small light steadies, so the viewer sees who was saved.

shots.camera: Static eye-level medium close-up, same framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Points of starlight appear one by one on the calm water on either side of Her and join into a line that runs away toward the horizon, which lights the water with a soft silver glow. The small light drifts slowly along the line, and the line carries it to a faint far shore light that answers with a steady glow. Her hand lowers slowly to Her side as the small light reaches the shore. In the last second the stars dim to a few points and the water returns to calm black, with Her third-eye glow steady.
shots.purpose: The star-and-ferry meaning: the guiding stars carry the small light across the water to a far shore, so the crossing is visible. The camera stays static so the star line and the travelling light are the only motion. The calm black ending matches the reference portrait, so the loop closes.

feedback: virality: Hook is strong in concept (huge rearing surge, small light at stake, frame 1 is the portrait), but the surge 'hangs trembling' above her shoulders for most of shot 1. A freeze-frame wave is close to a static pose for about 2 seconds. Real continuous motion is only the first beat, then a pause, then the palm.

virality: Whole clip is three static locked-off medium close-ups with a centered face. Visual variety is nil, so a 10s clip leans entirely on one small light and one star line. The small warm light at the bottom of the frame will be tiny on a phone screen and may not read as the stake.

virality: The palm beat is a generic raised-hand gesture. It is justified in the story only as a stand-in for her held objects, which is the 'gesture with no consequence' trap, even though here it does trigger the sea going flat. The third-eye-stops-surge beat before it makes the palm feel redundant: two causes for one effect.

virality: Violet-to-silver colour shift is the main 'poison' legibility device, and it is subtle on a small screen and compressed video. Viewers who don't know the myth will see a storm calming, not poison.

virality: Ending has a lot of stuff packed into 4 seconds (stars appear, light travels, shore answers, hand lowers, stars dim, water returns to black). Risk of mushy, rushed payoff. The loop depends on the dimming happening in the last second, which reads as anticlimax right at the end.

virality: Loop is good in concept (end frame = portrait = start frame), but the start is a surge already rearing while the end is calm black, so the replay jump is a cut from calm to chaos. This works as a hidden seam only if the surge arrives instantly, which is a hard cut.

virality: Send-worthiness is solid (friend in a dark stretch, 'you are the small light') and the caption gives a name-meaning fact to save, but save value is modest. Nothing here makes someone keep it beyond the one-line caption.

virality: Novelty is moderate. 'Goddess in front of a stormy sea, light path across water' is within the range of generic AI devotional clips. The distinct bits are the poison-violet glow and the third-eye stopping the wave.
virality: The reviewer notes about hair and held objects are production questions, not virality issues, and they bloat the concept.

authenticity: The palm-as-stand-in is not iconographic. The dossier lists scissors, skull cup, sword, blue lotus and knife, and an empty raised palm is invented. It is the only gesture in the clip and it carries the whole rescue beat. The concept at least flags this honestly for review.

authenticity: Loose hair is shipped knowingly. The dossier says it departs from the matted jata or Ekajata braid. Asking whether the anchor will be replaced is fair, but the shot text then adds a gravity-settling hair animation, which draws attention to the wrong detail. A devotee who knows Tara will notice.

authenticity: The clip tells the poison story visually (violet glow turning silver-blue) while the on-screen text is absent and the hedge sits only in the caption. Most viewers never read the caption, so the disputed legend plays as canonical. The 'sickly violet' poison coding also reads more like generic fantasy than Shiva's blue-throated halahala.

authenticity: The caption hedge is weak, a parenthetical at the end: '(In one devotional tradition, She calms the poisoned sea.)'. It does not say the story is outside the main Puranic accounts, and it does not flag that the goddess's identity varies by source.

authenticity: Ocean-of-samsara meaning is only implicit. The 'one small light' is an unexplained invented symbol, and the caption does not say what it stands for. The share trigger ('you are the small light') pushes it toward generic self-help rather than Tara's meaning.

authenticity: The third-eye 'glow brighter' that stops the surge reads as a laser-like superpower. The third eye in Tara iconography is not a weapon, and this edges toward fantasy-action framing. The 'stern unflinching' wrathful face is a good touch but the story leans heavily on spectacle.

authenticity: Cremation ground, corpse or Shiva-underfoot, and the tiger skin are absent from the beats, but the dossier does not require them, and omitting the corpse is a reasonable reverent choice.

feasibility: Far too many moving elements for one 10s clip. Surge rears on both sides of the head, a third-eye glow stops it, a small tossing light, hair settling, a palm lift, the whole sea flattening, a violet-to-silver colour shift, stars appearing one by one, a line forming toward the horizon, a light travelling along it, a far-shore light answering, the hand lowering, and stars dimming. That is a storyboard, not a single clip.

feasibility: The 'surge hangs trembling mid-rise' is a physically implausible freeze. Video models tend to let water either keep moving or collapse. It is also bad on the reference frame, because a huge surge on both sides of her head must appear from frame 1 against the calm portrait.

feasibility: Several beats read as one cause and effect but are two: the third eye glow 'stops' the surge, then the palm 'sinks' it. Third-eye glow brightening as a cause of a wave stopping is an abstract cause that the model will likely not render legibly.
feasibility: A mid-clip colour grade change (violet poison to silver-blue) tied to a gesture is hard to control. It will probably bleed or happen at the wrong moment.

feasibility: A small tossing light, 'stars appearing one by one', and 'a line joining' require precise sequential spawn timing. A tiny object travelling a path to a faint far shore light that 'answers' is too small and subtle to survive on a phone and likely to be dropped or jitter.

feasibility: Loop requires the final frame to return to the exact calm reference portrait after all that has happened, with the stars dimmed and the hand lowered. Fidelity to the first frame is unreliable. The first frame is also stated to be both the calm reference portrait and an already-risen surge, which conflicts.

feasibility: The hair settling 'gradually under gravity' while the sea surges is an unnecessary extra motion, and the water-line framing 'below her shoulders' with a surge on both sides of her head is a hard composition to hold stable.
feasibility: Shot-by-shot hard descriptions imply three shots with a static camera, which is fine, but the clip is one continuous render, so the 3/3/4 timings will not be obeyed precisely.

virality fix: Cut the hanging-surge beat. Have the surge keep visibly rolling and cresting toward the light for the first 2s, and let the third eye flash arrest it only in the last half-second before the palm, so there is never a held frame.

virality fix: Make the small light larger, brighter and a clearly different warm colour from the violet sea, and place it a little higher in the frame so it is readable at thumbnail size and not lost under a chin-height crop.

virality fix: Collapse the double cause: either the third-eye pulse or the palm ends the surge, not both. Prefer the palm for the physical consequence and use the third eye as a flare on the same beat.
virality fix: Add a camera move on the settle (a slow push-in or a small shake that stills on the palm) to give the payoff weight, and to separate the three beats visually.

virality fix: Simplify the last shot: stars appear and carry the light to the shore, and make that the final peak. Drop the separate hand-lowering and stars-dimming business so the clip does not end on a fade-out. Let the calm-black reset happen with one quick dim into the opening.

virality fix: Make the loop seam an intentional hard cut on the conch note: end on the calm portrait with the far light still glowing, and open on the surge slamming up with the same low rumble, so the restart feels like an event, not a reset.
virality fix: Strengthen the save hook with a short visible reason to keep it (for example, the caption lists the three meanings of Tara as star, saviour and ferrier in a saveable format).
virality fix: Move the reviewer-notes content out of the concept body so the story field is only about what viewers will see.

authenticity fix: Rework the caption so it names the hedge plainly: 'A devotional tradition (not in the main Puranic accounts) tells of Tara calming the poison from the churning of the ocean.' Make it the first or second line, not a trailing parenthetical.

authenticity fix: Replace or supplement the bare palm with one iconographic object, for example a blue lotus held in the raised hand, which is non-graphic, easy to render and in the dossier's list. Alternatively keep the palm but add the lotus or scissors in a single beat and say so in the caption.
authenticity fix: Do not animate the hair. Keep it still, or swap the anchor to Ekajata or matted jata before final. Do not showcase a known deviation.

authenticity fix: Tone down the violet glow. Use dark, heavy water with a faint dark current, as in the dossier's recommended beat, and make the third-eye glow steady rather than brightening as an attack, so the gaze reads as presence and not a beam.
authenticity fix: Name the small light in the caption ('a devotee, anyone in the dark') so it is clearly a stand-in and not a claimed canonical element.
feasibility fix: Cut it to three elements: the water surge, the palm lift, and a single path of light. Drop the far-shore answer, the colour shift, the hair motion, and the stars-dim ending.
feasibility fix: Remove the 'hangs mid-rise' freeze. Let the surge rise slowly behind her, then subside as the palm lifts, with a clear cause (palm up, water flattens).
feasibility fix: Replace the third-eye 'stops the wave' causality with the palm alone being the cause. Keep the third eye as a constant glow.
feasibility fix: Make the small light larger and keep it near the lower centre. Use one continuous glowing line, not stars appearing one by one.
feasibility fix: Drop the exact-match loop requirement. End on a calm, settled water state that is close to the portrait, and accept a soft seam.
feasibility fix: Choose a single colour for the water (dark blue-black with a faint violet rim) and avoid the transition.
